rubric.note: Subjective internal editorial ratings with evidence; not an automatic humour metric or an independent live review.

card.title: Warmly Withholding
card.instruction: Remain open, caring, and reassuring while revealing less with every new question.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your school meeting went fine, love. The headteacher and I discussed your suspension. Have some tea.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How long am I suspended?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A little while. I'll be home with you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will I miss the school play?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Oh, sweetheart. Come sit beside me. You don't have to face this alone.

card.title: Warmly Withholding
card.instruction: Remain open, caring, and reassuring while revealing less with every new question.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your wedding dress reached our depot this morning. Please sit; I'll look after you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Which depot? I'll collect it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One of ours. Let me save you a wasted journey.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can you at least give me their number?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You have me, and I'm staying right here with you.

card.title: Secrets Have Value
card.instruction: Price every fact, introduction, warning, and confession as something that must be traded for equal value.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll name the coworker who reported your lateness if you name whoever reported mine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only know which department.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll trade departments. Names cost names.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Payroll. But I can introduce you to my source.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Marketing. And I'll arrange coffee with mine. Same access, same price.

card.title: Secrets Have Value
card.instruction: Price every fact, introduction, warning, and confession as something that must be traded for equal value.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll tell you why I took Mum's spare key if you admit something that could get you grounded too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I broke her mug.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's a weekend. This key is a month. Have you got anything bigger?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I lent her car to Jamie.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A month each, then. I used the key to let Jamie move into her flat.

card.title: I Told You Enough
card.instruction: Agree to be honest while repeatedly narrowing what honesty requires and which details count.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll be honest about your missing donation box. You asked where I went; I said the bank.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Did you take the box there?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. You didn't ask what was inside.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Was the money still in it when you arrived?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: At the car park, yes. If you mean the counter, that's a different arrival.

card.title: I Told You Enough
card.instruction: Agree to be honest while repeatedly narrowing what honesty requires and which details count.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll give you an honest account of my birthday dinner. I said no guests; nobody was invited.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your brother posted a photo from our kitchen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: He has a key. Family letting themselves in aren't guests.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He's holding a cake that says 'Welcome, guests.'

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll answer for what I told you. The baker's account is separate.

card.title: The Conspiracy Expands
card.instruction: Use every denial, coincidence, and missing detail as proof that more people and higher stakes are involved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our toaster receipt is gone. The shop must have someone inside this house.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I probably recycled it. We can get a copy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So the recycling crew removes originals while the shop prints replacements.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Every shop prints replacement receipts.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Every shop? Then it's the whole high street. We can't trust a single warranty.

card.title: The Conspiracy Expands
card.instruction: Use every denial, coincidence, and missing detail as proof that more people and higher stakes are involved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You and your manager both say my train was cancelled. Who told you to match stories?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The signal failed. It's on the public departure board.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They've recruited the board operators to stop me reaching the interview.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The same fault is delaying three counties.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Three counties to keep me unemployed. My replacement must already have government backing.

card.title: Help Me Make This Normal
card.instruction: Get someone to help perform the strange behavior until it feels ordinary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Pass the talking cupboard a napkin. Let's make dinner normal.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It doesn't have a lap.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then put it beside the handle, like a considerate host.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Should I offer it soup?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please. Ask which shelf it eats from. We can't keep making our guest explain everything.

card.title: Help Me Make This Normal
card.instruction: Get someone to help perform the strange behavior until it feels ordinary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Say hello to the invisible guest without staring.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can't see where to look.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Look at the chair. That's where visible guests usually begin.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Hello, chair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good start. Ask whether the guest wants the window open.

card.title: You Can’t Leave Mid-Prophecy
card.instruction: Keep someone present until the impossible prediction has been fulfilled, disproved, or responsibly revised.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stay until sunset. Gran predicted this stone would hatch, and I promised we'd witness the result.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The sun's down. It's still a stone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then help me record that it didn't hatch. We can put the prophecy to rest.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll sign, but Gran never said which day.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then stay while we ring her and agree a deadline. I can't witness every sunset alone.

card.title: You Can’t Leave Mid-Prophecy
card.instruction: Keep someone present until the impossible prediction has been fulfilled, disproved, or responsibly revised.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep your coat off. The prophecy says this bell-less tower will ring at noon; I need a witness.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's twelve-oh-one. We heard nothing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then sign that before you go. We can officially stop waiting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My watch is five minutes fast.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then give me four more minutes. I'll fill in our names so only the silence needs witnessing.

card.title: Apologize to Reality
card.instruction: Get someone to apologize to an object, rule, place, or idea for violating its impossible expectations.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Apologise to the chair. You sat before it agreed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a chair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then a brief apology should be easy.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sorry, chair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For what? Furniture appreciates specificity.

card.title: Apologize to Reality
card.instruction: Get someone to apologize to an object, rule, place, or idea for violating its impossible expectations.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Apologise to the doorway before trying the handle. You entered without letting it arrive first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was already here. It's attached to the house.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. It can't go ahead unless you make allowances.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sorry I didn't carry you in first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. Promise you'll wait on the step next time until it feels it has led the way.

card.title: Approve the Impossible Plan
card.instruction: Get someone to formally approve a plan whose logic becomes stranger each time it is explained.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Approve storing Tuesday's rain in this cup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Tuesday hasn't happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which is why we have room.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What happens if it overflows?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll borrow a saucer from Wednesday. Sign here.

card.title: Approve the Impossible Plan
card.instruction: Get someone to formally approve a plan whose logic becomes stranger each time it is explained.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sign off on the invisible landing before we build the stairs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's nothing there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No visible defects. An excellent inspection result.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How do we stand on it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: With confidence included in the materials budget.

card.title: You Handle the Impossible Part
card.instruction: Make someone accept responsibility for the one part of the plan that cannot reasonably be done.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You fold the moon; I'll stack these chairs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How do I fold the moon?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start with the crescent. It already suggests a crease.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why do you get chairs?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Someone must keep the achievable work moving.

card.title: You Handle the Impossible Part
card.instruction: Make someone accept responsibility for the one part of the plan that cannot reasonably be done.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put yesterday's missing hour in this jar before lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Time doesn't fit in jars.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then loosen the lid. Don't make the opening smaller than necessary.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You do it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm labelling. We mustn't confuse it with tomorrow.

card.title: What Rule Did I Miss?
card.instruction: Find the hidden rule that makes the strange situation consistent, practical, or at least survivable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: What keeps the soup inside that upside-down bowl?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've never seen it either.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then turn the spoon over. Let's test which thing owns down.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The soup followed the spoon.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the spoon sets the direction. Point it into the sink before we try putting it down.

card.title: What Rule Did I Miss?
card.instruction: Find the hidden rule that makes the strange situation consistent, practical, or at least survivable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your shadow moved before you. What changed?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was walking slowly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stop completely. Let's see whether it waits.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's heading for the door.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then destination outranks speed. Follow without changing anything else.
